newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.

text.p: The Malaysian interbank money market and interest rates futures market, the Malaysia Monetary Exchange, were closed on Thursday to observe the Labour Day.
On Wednesday, the interbank market closed with a sharp improvement in liquidity, though some late cover pushed up the overnight rate to the upper limit of 8.7 percent.
Dealers said some big banks were borrowing just before the close. Most of the deals were earlier done at 5.8/6.00 percent.
Short-term interbank rates fell earlier as liquidity improved further due to the maturity of a 420 million ringgit long-term government bond issue, dealers said.
One-week money was at 6.5/8 percent against 6.80/7.00 on Tuesday, two-week at 7.00/10 percent against 7.10/20 and three-week at 7.10/20 percent against 7.10/25.
One-month money at 7.20/25 percent, three-month at 7.25/30 percent and six-month at 7.30/35 percent, were all steady.
They said the interbank rates were expected to fall further as more funds were expected to come in. On Friday, there is a maturity of 500 million ringgit in Bank Negara bills.
